why: One light board: a browser card on the left with a login form and a Submit button, a server card on the right, a path between them with a router box and a watcher marker on it. On Submit, a packet carrying the readable form fields leaves the browser along the path.
The packet passes the watcher, which duplicates it; the copy shows the same readable form fields, held beside the original so both read identically.
The same board holds still; a small open padlock icon appears above the path, promising the outcome, without changing the layout.
A request arrow runs from browser to server; a certificate card slides back to the browser showing a domain name and a key, and an authority seal appears on the words 'signed by'.
On the certificate card at the browser, three ticks appear one at a time beside signer, name and dates, each on its phrase.
The certificate card shrinks to a ticked badge; an empty key slot appears at each end of the path, with the watcher still between them.
Two small value tokens cross the path in opposite directions; the watcher copies each into a tray, and a blank key slot stays empty beside the watcher.
Matching keys appear in the slots at browser and server only; the watcher's slot remains empty.
The ticked badge enlarges beside the keys and its three ticks re-light in turn, tying the key to the passed check.
The form data block at the browser, readable, passes through the key and turns into scrambled blocks as it leaves.
Scrambled blocks travel past the watcher, whose copy is the same unreadable pattern.
At the server the scrambled blocks pass the key and turn readable again.
